# Measured native compatibility reference

`native-numeric.json` freezes **actual original native execution**, not expected
values generated by the new TCPCI mapper. The reference wheel was built from
public source `1edbee874129aa85e26e592d9649826e85e1ac6b` (4.20.0); all 358 SDK
resources were checked against that source before installation into a clean
external standard-library venv. The fixture records the resulting wheel hash,
driver hash, selected numeric dependency versions and producer platform.

The input is the existing authored, twelve-row
`tests/fixtures/native-semantics/v1/legacy-ci-inputs.json`. It is constructed CI
data, not a claim of independently observed builds, faults or policy advantage.
Eight real YAML → `load_spec` → `api.run` → runner → Parquet cases cover Random
and UCB/RNFail with ratio budgets 0.5/1, three modeled seconds and two tests.
Each case contains four native rows and the complete three-test order/hash.

The comparison covers the explicit 22-field logical projection. `fitness` is
dimensionless NAPFD and `cost` is dimensionless APFDc; neither is time or money.
Recorded test durations model additive reported work, not physical runner time.
When no failure is detected, the original `ttf_duration` fallback retains the
full modeled suite duration; the independent reference instead represents the
censored first-failure time as unavailable. The compatibility test preserves
that difference rather than changing old data.

Measured process resources, timings and physical execution IDs remain excluded
from exact numeric comparison. Their names are retained per case. The digest is
over canonical JSON of the projected rows, not over the complete Parquet bytes,
installed producer image, mutable workspace or executable checkpoint. New
runtime provenance is expected to differ. Old readable artifacts acquire no
verified execution attribution or additional units from this fixture.

`tests/tcpci_compatibility/test_native_numeric.py` checks the frozen rows with
the existing independent rational metric reference, then compares a newly
installed current CI wheel against them. Assertions never regenerate the golden
on mismatch. Other native names retain their separate source/catalog/installed
matrix qualification; this small profile does not establish universal trace
determinism, especially for the separately disclosed FRRMAB route.

To inspect one reference case, build the pinned source into its own wheel,
install it into a fresh environment with the fixture's exact numeric pins, and
copy the current `native_driver.py` and original input JSON outside the checkout.
Run the copied driver there, with a new output directory:

```console
/path/to/pinned-reference/bin/python -I -B native_driver.py \
  legacy-ci-inputs.json /outside/reference-case Random ratio 0.5
```

The driver requires a noneditable installed package, writes ordinary native
configuration/provenance/results, and emits its own receipt only after all four
rows and ranking hashes validate. Keep the original wheel, dependency lock and
trusted executable state when continuing an old experiment; matching this
numeric projection is not checkpoint or workspace migration.
